title: HUL tells Delhi High Court it will remove Lakme sunscreen ad disparaging Derma Co
summary: Hindustan Unilever Limited told the Delhi High Court it will withdraw and republish Lakme sunscreen advertisements after removing references that allegedly disparage Honasa Consumer Limited’s Derma Co brand.
content:
Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL), owner of the Lakme brand, informed the Delhi High Court on Thursday that it will withdraw and republish its Lakme sunscreen advertisements after removing references that allegedly disparage Honasa Consumer Limited’s Derma Co brand.

The company said it would take down the current ads and issue revised versions without the contested references. HUL told the court the changes would address the complaints made by Honasa Consumer Limited regarding alleged disparagement of the Derma Co brand.

The matter was brought before the Delhi High Court, where HUL recorded its intention to modify and republish the advertisements rather than continue with the existing creative copy that prompted the dispute.

## Incident Details

Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL), owner of the Lakme brand, informed the Delhi High Court on Thursday that it will withdraw and republish its Lakme sunscreen advertisements after removing references that allegedly disparage Honasa Consumer Limited’s Derma Co brand.

## HUL’s Response

The company said it would take down the current ads and issue revised versions without the contested references. HUL told the court the changes would address the complaints made by Honasa Consumer Limited regarding alleged disparagement of the Derma Co brand.

- Take down current advertisements
- Issue revised versions without the contested references
- Address Honasa Consumer Limited’s complaints

## Legal Proceedings

The matter was brought before the Delhi High Court, where HUL recorded its intention to modify and republish the advertisements rather than continue with the existing creative copy that prompted the dispute.
